title: China's CXMT Rejects Apple Request for Below-Market DRAM Pricing
summary:
CXMT declined a request from Apple to provide memory chips at prices below the current market rate, according to a market report. The decision underscores the current leverage of the Chinese DRAM producer as a shortage of artificial intelligence memory chips continues to drive pricing higher across the industry.

The refusal follows a surge in CXMT's third-quarter revenue to about $16.7B, a 613% increase year over year, and a net profit of $8.17B. For the first nine months of the year, the chipmaker's revenue reached $40.39B with a net income of $19.82B, although sequential quarterly profit growth of only 3% suggests that the pace of price gains is cooling.

selectedTweets.text:
China's biggest DRAM maker just printed one of the most insane quarters in the entire chip industry.

CXMT did about $16.7 billion in revenue last quarter, up 613% from a year ago.

Net profit came in at about $8.17 billion.

It also turned down a request from Apple for below market DRAM pricing and that tells you exactly who has the leverage right now.

The one warning sign is that profit only grew about 3% from the prior quarter, so price gains are starting to slow even as the shortage continues.

Micron $MU has fallen 50% or more 10 separate times since 1995.

Every one of those drops:

→ 1995-96: -82%
→ 1997-98: -66%
→ 1999: -57%
→ 2000-01: -82%
→ 2002-03: -83%
→ 2006-08: -91%
→ 2011: -63%
→ 2014-16: -74%
→ 2018: -54%
→ 2024-25: -58%

The worst took the stock from $18.57 in September 2006 to $1.69 in November 2008.

The most recent ran from June 2024 to April 2025, when it bottomed at $64.72. Micron is up more than 10x from that low.

Memory chip prices swing hard with supply and demand, and Micron's profits swing with them.
